title: Styling with CSS
examples: How do I make all my headings blue?
What is the difference between an ID selector and a class selector?
Can CSS change the spacing between words?

explain.say: Today we are learning about CSS for styling web pages. CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.
First we look at selectors. Selectors tell CSS what element to style. You can select by element name like p or h1.
Next we learn about colours. You can change text colour using the color property. For example, setting the color to blue.
Layout basics help position elements on the page. The display property controls how an element behaves. For instance, changing it to block.
For a real-life example consider a school notice board. You use CSS selectors to target specific signs. You use the color property to make important text stand out.
A common mistake is forgetting to close your curly braces. Remember that every rule set needs its opening and closing braces.

items: And always check your closing brace }.

faq.q: How do I change the background colour of a section?
faq.a: You use the background-color property for this. You apply it just like you apply the color property to text.
asks: How do I colour the whole box?

faq.q: What is the difference between an ID and a class?
faq.a: An ID is for one unique element only on a page. A class can be used on many different elements.
asks: Can I use the same class twice?
When should I use an ID selector?

faq.a: Inline elements only take up as much space as their content needs. They sit next to other text easily.
asks: What is the difference between block and inline?

faq.q: Do I need to write CSS in a separate file?
faq.a: It is best practice to keep your CSS in a separate file. This keeps your code clean and organized.
asks: Where should I put my styles?
Is it okay to put styles in the HTML?

faq.q: How do I select an image specifically?
faq.a: You can select images using an attribute selector or by giving the image an ID. This targets that specific picture.
asks: Can I target an image tag?
What if I want to style only one picture?

facts: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.
The color property sets text or background colours.
Display properties control element layout like block or inline.

quiz.say: Which CSS property changes the text colour of an element?
quiz.why: The color property is specifically designed to set the foreground colour, which is usually the text.

wrong.0: This property controls if the text is italic or normal, not its actual colour.
wrong.1: This is not a standard CSS property name, so the browser will not recognize it.
wrong.3: This property changes the entire background area, not just the text itself.

quiz.say: To make a heading take up the full width available, which display value should you use?
quiz.why: The block display type forces an element to start on a new line and take up all available horizontal space.

wrong.1: Inline elements only take up the space necessary for their content, sitting next to other items.
wrong.2: Flex is a layout model, but 'block' is the fundamental value for full width.
wrong.3: While this often works, 'block' is the fundamental display setting that guarantees this behavior.

quiz.say: If you want to style only one specific paragraph on a page, which selector method is best?
quiz.why: ID selectors are meant to target one unique element, ensuring your style only applies where you intend it to.

wrong.1: This will style every single paragraph on the entire webpage, not just one.
wrong.2: A class selector can be used on multiple elements, so it is not guaranteed to be unique.
wrong.3: This selector targets every single element on the page, which is too broad.
